documents.title: Shareholder Meeting / Postal Ballot-Outcome of AGM
INTIMATION FOR RESCHEDULING OF 60TH ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING OF THE COMPANY ON 26TH AUGUST 2026 (WEDNESDAY) AT 12:00 NOON (IST)

analysis.summary: Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited (CPCL) achieved its highest ever annual crude throughput of 11.71 MMT for FY26, representing 112% of its installed capacity. The company reported a gross refining margin (GRM) of $9.2 per barrel for the full year and $13.75 per barrel for the fourth quarter. CPCL recommended a record total dividend of INR 62 per share, including a final dividend of INR 54 per share. Looking ahead, the company is executing INR 2,000 crores of capital projects, including Group 2 and 3 LOBS and retail outlet expansions, over the next 2 to 3 years. Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited reported its Q4 FY25 and full year financial and operational performance, highlighting strong physical performance despite scheduled maintenance shutdowns.

guidance.claim: CPCL expects a lot of commissioning of retail outlets in the year '26-'27.
guidance.quote: Even our retail outlet endeavor for which we had taken 300 licenses has started. And this year, that is '26-'27, we'll see a lot of commissioning out of them.

guidance.claim: CPCL hopes to complete its ongoing debottlenecking study in the coming year '26-'27.
guidance.quote: But in the coming year, '26-'27, we hope that ongoing study will get completed.

guidance.claim: CPCL expects the momentum of resilient operational and financial performance to continue in the new financial year.
guidance.quote: To summarize, we continue to deliver resilient operational and financial performance and see the momentum to continue in the new financial year as well.

demand_outlook.claim: CPCL noted that global uncertainties are affecting the availability of LPG all over the world.
demand_outlook.quote: With global uncertainties affecting the availability of LPG all over the world, CPCL is happy to step up the requirement when the nation needed it.

demand_outlook.claim: CPCL stated that cracks for diesel and ATF are reasonable and close to long-term averages.
demand_outlook.quote: But still in these months, the cracks are reasonable enough and close to our long-term averages.

demand_outlook.claim: CPCL stated that the long-term average for GRM is around $13 per barrel.
demand_outlook.quote: I found around 13 $/bbl to be the long-term average.

demand_outlook.claim: Management stated that the southern market for motor spirit (MS) exhibits a shortfall where production is less than demand.
demand_outlook.quote: MS in southern market, there is a clear shortfall so, the production is less than demand.

demand_outlook.claim: Management noted that the southern market for MS is projecting around 4%-5% growth while HSD has a 3% growth forecast.
demand_outlook.quote: Like MS, they are projecting 6% and here we see around 4%-5%. HSD we see at 3% growth forecast, as against 2.5% odd here.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL's capex during the current year was INR 856 crores compared to INR 673 crores in the previous year.
capex_expansion.quote: During the current year, the capex was INR856 crores as compared to INR673 crores in the previous year.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL has started project execution for Group 2, Group 3 LOBS and its retail outlet endeavor.
capex_expansion.quote: Some of the important projects that we'll be taking up is Group 2, Group 3 LOBS for which all approvals are in place and the project execution has started in full swing.

capex_expansion.claim: The Group 2, Group 3 LOBS project is INR 1,600 crores and the retail outlet project is INR 400 crores, totaling INR 2,000 crores over 2 to 3 years.
capex_expansion.quote: LOBS project, Group 2, Group 3 LOBS project is INR1,600 crores. The retail outlet project is INR400 crores. So that makes it INR2,000 crores. This INR2,000 crores will happen over 2 to 3 years.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL expects a normal capex of another INR 500 crores every year.
capex_expansion.quote: Besides, every year, you can assume another INR500 crores is our normal capex.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL is studying low-cost debottlenecking or enhancement in secondary processes with EIL.
capex_expansion.quote: And we are talking to EIL idea is that when we are consistently able to perform at this level, can we implement some debottlenecking or enhancement in our secondary processes on a systematic basis with low-cost capex?

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL spent Rs. 673 crores as capex for the financial year.
capex_expansion.quote: On the CAPEX front, in the current year, we have spent Rs. 673 crores as CAPEX for the current year.

capex_expansion.claim: The revised capital cost for the CBR project is Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian oil respectively.
capex_expansion.quote: The revised capital cost is at Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian oil respectively.

capex_expansion.claim: The new refinery has a capacity of 9 million metric tons with a petrochemical intensity of 6% for polypropylene.
capex_expansion.quote: The new refinery capital cost is Rs 36,000 Crore approximately, 9 million metric ton capacity and petrochemical intensity of 6% and which is PP, polypropylene.

margins_costs.claim: CPCL's gross refining margin (GRM) for FY25-26 was $9.2 per barrel compared to the Singapore benchmark of $5.83 per barrel.
margins_costs.quote: The gross refining margin, GRM, for financial year 2025- '26 was $9.2 per barrel as compared to Singapore benchmark of $5.83 per barrel.

margins_costs.claim: The GRM for Q4 was $13.75 per barrel compared to the Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for quarter 4 was $13.75 barrel as compared to Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel, which again reiterates that all these efficiencies are constant, continuous and are being sustained over each period.

margins_costs.claim: CPCL's core GRM for Q4 was $10.3 per barrel.
CPCL's niche products contribute around 15% of its margins.
margins_costs.quote: About 7% to 8% constitutes these kinds of niche products. And this 7%–8% is currently contributing around 15% of my margins.

margins_costs.claim: CPCL achieved its best fuel and loss of 7.73% in the current financial year.
margins_costs.quote: CPCL achieved the best fuel and loss of 7.73%, best MBN of 69.8% and best EII of 84% in the current financial year '25-'26, surpassing our previous best records achieved in the last financial year, this was driven by the effective implementation of energy conservation initiatives and significantly improved operational reliability.

margins_costs.claim: Inventory gain for the fourth quarter was $0.66 per barrel, amounting to Rs. 125 crores.
margins_costs.quote: Yes, the inventory gain is not very significant for the quarter. It is only $ 0.66 per barrel. And in absolute rupee terms, it is Rs. 125 crores only.

margins_costs.claim: On a full year basis, the inventory showed a loss of $0.06 per barrel or Rs. 40 crores.
margins_costs.quote: But on an overall annual basis, the inventory would be a loss that is $ 0.06 per barrel, Rs. 40 crores in amount.

margins_costs.claim: The company reported a total GRM of $3.40 per barrel for 9M 2024-25.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved its highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, equivalent to 112% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, million metric ton, which equivalents to 112% of installed capacity, breaking records of our previous best of 11.64 MMT achieved in financial year 2023-'24.

orders_capacity.claim: In Q4, CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, which is 111% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: In quarter 4 of the current financial year, CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, which is also 111% of installed capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved highest ever production levels of 5.139 MMT for diesel and 1.318 MMT for petrol.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL concluded the financial year on a high note, achieving the highest ever production levels of 5.139 MMT for diesel HSD, and 1.318 MMT of petrol that is MS, an impressive testament of the refinery's outstanding operational performance.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved its highest ever distillate yield of 79.1%.
orders_capacity.quote: Further, highest ever distillate yield of 79.1%, beating our previous record of 77.6% set in 2019-'20 was also achieved during this year.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved highest ever LPG production of 447 TMT.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved highest ever LPG production of 447 TMT, overcoming previous record of 404 set in 2023-'24.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT, which is equivalent to 99.5% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT, equivalent to 99.5% of our installed capacity and this must be seen with respect to the turnaround that has happened during the year

orders_capacity.claim: Crude throughput for Quarter 4 was 2.974 MMT, representing 113% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: and coming on to Quarter 4, the crude throughput was 2.974, which is 113% of installed capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: The installed capacity of the Manali Refinery is 10.5 MMTPA.

capital_allocation.claim: CPCL's debt equity ratio stands at 0.18 at a gross level and 0.09 on a net basis.
capital_allocation.quote: Our debt equity stands at 0.18 at a gross level as compared to 0.39 last year.

capital_allocation.claim: CPCL's gross borrowings are INR 1,900 crores, and net borrowings are INR 973 crores.
capital_allocation.quote: On a gross basis, the borrowings are INR1,900 crores, but on a net basis, it is less than INR1,000 crores, to be precise, INR973 crores.

capital_allocation.claim: CPCL recommended a final dividend of INR 54 per share in addition to an interim dividend of INR 8 per share, totaling INR 62 per share.
capital_allocation.quote: During the year, for the first time, CPCL paid an interim dividend, and we are happy to announce that in addition to the interim dividend of INR8 per equity share of INR10 each, the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR54 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to INR62 per share, which again is highest ever.

capital_allocation.claim: The board recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share, representing 50% of the face value.
capital_allocation.quote: With the above, the Board has also recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share that is 50% of face value for the current year and as we all know, this is subject to approval at AGM, which will happen in the due course.

capital_allocation.claim: Total debt as on March 31, 2025 stood at Rs. 3,100 crores with a net worth of Rs. 7,939 crores.
capital_allocation.quote: At an absolute level, the debt stands at Rs. 3,100 crores as compared to Rs. 2,762 crores as on March 31, 2024. Net worth is at Rs. 7,939 crores as on March 31, 2025.

risks_headwinds.claim: CPCL noted that logistical constraints and volatility of crude oil prices pose challenges.
risks_headwinds.quote: Now with all this, I would like to say the uncertainties due to logistical constraints, volatility of crude oil prices do pose challenges.

risks_headwinds.claim: CPCL experienced a forex loss of approximately INR 200 crores for the quarter and around INR 350 crores for the whole year.
risks_headwinds.quote: For the quarter, it would be for the quarter, it is approximately INR 200 crores,. And for the whole year, it will be around INR350 crores.

risks_headwinds.claim: CPCL has a scheduled maintenance and inspection of one of its refinery units close to September or October.
risks_headwinds.quote: But yes, maybe close to September, October, we have a scheduled M&I of one of our refinery units.

risks_headwinds.claim: CPCL experienced a 30% to 40% disturbance in Middle East cargo flows over a short period.
risks_headwinds.quote: What has impacted is that maybe 30% to 40% was affected over a very short period, but all have assured us that depending on the situation, they will make up all the cargoes.

risks_headwinds.claim: Management stated that uncertainties due to the volatility of crude prices pose a challenge.
risks_headwinds.quote: Finally, the uncertainties due to volatility of crude prices do pose a challenge.

management_commitments.claim: CPCL expects a lot of commissioning of retail outlets in the year '26-'27.
management_commitments.quote: Even our retail outlet endeavor for which we had taken 300 licenses has started. And this year, that is '26-'27, we'll see a lot of commissioning out of them.

management_commitments.claim: CPCL will execute the LOBS and retail outlet projects over 2 to 3 years.
management_commitments.quote: This INR2,000 crores will happen over 2 to 3 years.

management_commitments.claim: CPCL has a scheduled maintenance and inspection of one of its refinery units close to September or October.
management_commitments.quote: But yes, maybe close to September, October, we have a scheduled M&I of one of our refinery units.

management_commitments.claim: CPCL hopes to complete its ongoing debottlenecking study in the coming year '26-'27.
management_commitments.quote: But in the coming year, '26-'27, we hope that ongoing study will get completed.

management_commitments.claim: Management stated that maintenance capex for the next year is forecasted to remain in the range of Rs. 200-250 crores.
management_commitments.quote: Our maintenance CAPEX remains Rs. 200-250 crore range, and the next year forecast also, we feel the CAPEX will be in that range.

management_commitments.claim: Management stated that normal maintenance capex for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores.
management_commitments.quote: The normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores, maintenance CAPEX plus small regular CAPEX normally.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
